display.title: Hashem's Name: Rabbi Moshe Galanti and the Sheikh's Secret, Part 1 (Lech Lecha)
display.summary_short: Why does the Torah begin Avraham's story at age 75? A Lech Lecha teaching on doing mitzvos because Hashem said so, and the start of a mysterious story from Damascus.
display.summary_long: For Parshas Lech Lecha, the storyteller asks why the written Torah tells nothing of Avraham's first 75 years, though the Midrash has many stories: recognizing Hashem at three, breaking the idols, surviving Nimrod's furnace. One answer the Rebbe gives is that Avraham became a Jew only when Hashem first commanded him, "Lech Lecha." Until then he did good because his own heart and mind told him to; a Jew does good because Hashem said so. Doing a mitzvah such as honoring parents only when we feel like it works on Sunday but not on Monday; doing it because Hashem commanded is steady every day. The words "go away from your land" also mean leaving one's own will and habits behind. Then the story begins: over 300 years ago in Damascus, Rabbi Moshe Galanti hears that the local Arab sheikh can always tell whether a sick person will live. Determined to learn the secret, he arranges a visit through the community leader, impresses the sheikh with his knowledge of the seven wisdoms, and is invited back twice a week, waiting for the right moment to ask. To be continued.
display.lesson: A Jew does mitzvos because Hashem commanded them, not only when he feels like it, and so keeps doing good every day.
